# Datasets Used in This Book {#sec-datasets}

The book uses two kinds of data: datasets that come with R and its packages, which are convenient for showing how a function works, and data simulated for this book, which carry the audit examples.

## Datasets that come with R {#sec-builtin-data}

The following datasets are available in every installation of R. Their descriptions below are taken from R's own help pages.

::: {.cell}

:::


- `anscombe`:
     Four x-y datasets which have the same traditional statistical
     properties (mean, variance, correlation, regression line, etc.), yet
     are quite different.

- `iris`:
     This famous (Fisher's or Anderson's) iris data set gives the
     measurements in centimeters of the variables sepal length and width and
     petal length and width, respectively, for 50 flowers from each of 3

- `nhtemp`:
     The mean annual temperature in degrees Fahrenheit in New Haven,
     Connecticut, from 1912 to 1971.

- `Nile`:
     Measurements of the annual flow of the river Nile at Aswan (formerly
     'Assuan'), 1871-1970, in 10^8 m^3, "with apparent changepoint near
     1898" (Cobb(1978), Table 1, p.249).

## Data simulated for this book {#sec-ssydata}

Most audit examples use data simulated in R, because real audit data cannot be published. The data is made to look like what auditors receive, and irregularities are *planted* in it for the analysis to find. All names of persons, firms, offices and places are made up, and do not relate to any real entity.

In most chapters, the code that creates the data is shown, folded, at the start of the example, so that readers can see exactly what was planted, change it, and run it again. The table lists these datasets, chapter by chapter, in the order of the book. Chapters which use only a few values typed in by hand are left out.

### The Sarvajan Swasthya Yojana data {.unnumbered}

Several chapters share one larger dataset, for an imaginary State health insurance scheme, *Sarvajan Swasthya Yojana* (SSY). They are the chapters on principal components (@sec-pca), clustering (@sec-kmeans), association rules (@sec-apriori), text (@sec-text, @sec-sentiment and @sec-textviz), maps (@sec-maps) and Benford's Law (@sec-benford). The last chapter of Part IX, @sec-ssyaudit, brings all of them together in one audit. Its files are in the `Data` folder of the book's repository. The code that creates them is in `tools/make_health_scheme_data.R`, `tools/make_ssy_text_data.R` and `tools/make_ssy_geo_data.R`.

| File | One row per | Main columns |
|-------------------|----------------|----------------------------------------|
| `ssy_hospitals.csv` | Empanelled hospital | `hospital_id`, `hospital_name`, `type` (Public or Private), `district`, `beds` |
| `ssy_packages.csv` | Treatment package | `package_code`, `package_name`, `specialty`, `rate`, `surgical`, `day_care`, `typical_los` |
| `ssy_claims.csv` | Claim paid in 2024-25 | `claim_id`, `hospital_id`, `patient_id`, `gender`, `age`, `admission_date`, `discharge_date`, `packages` (codes separated by `;`, main package first), `claim_amount` |
| `ssy_grievances.csv` | Grievance filed against a hospital | `grievance_id`, `received_on`, `district`, `hospital_id`, `category`, `text` |
| `ssy_feedback.csv` | Comment left by a patient | `feedback_id`, `hospital_id`, `comment`, `rating` |
| `ssy_map.gpkg` | Map layer | The State and its districts |
| `ssy_hospital_locations.csv` | Empanelled hospital | `hospital_id`, `x_km`, `y_km` |
| `ssy_patient_homes.csv` | Claim | `claim_id`, `hospital_id`, `home_x_km`, `home_y_km` |
| `ssy_inspections.csv` | Inspection of a hospital | `hospital_id`, `inspection_no`, `inspection_date`, `inspector`, `photo_x_km`, `photo_y_km` |

: Files of the SSY dataset {#tbl-ssyfiles}

Planted in it are six hospitals behaving like "camps" (high claims per bed, short stays, weekend admissions, repeated admissions, unbundled packages) and two hospitals upcoding to intensive care, which the chapters find in different ways. The text and map files carry the same story. Grievances and feedback complain about the camp hospitals, their patients come from far away, and some inspection photos were taken far from the hospital.
